source_review.notes: Checked the Reactive Streams specification/site, current Apache Flink backpressure/network/checkpoint/recovery documentation, current Spark Kafka admission controls, Kafka producer/consumer/quota documentation, and TCP RFC 9293. All thirteen cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Product-specific controls/metrics are attributed and separated from general queueing and boundedness claims.

evidence: Reviewed arrival lambda_i, service mu_i, backlog q_i, capacity K_i, expansion f_i/g_i, utilization rho, mean population L, mean time W, and recovery backlog N.
Checked records/s, bytes/s, work/s, records/bytes, seconds, MB, queue capacity, and catch-up capacity use explicit dimensions.
Checked offered versus admitted rate and blocked/rejected/shed terminal outcomes are distinguished in conservation equations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Little's relation is scoped to stable consistent averages and explicitly not applied to percentiles or used as a stability proof.

evidence: Executed bounded-queue-overload with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced offered 1500, processed 1200, queued 200, blocked/rejected 100, conservation true, and three drain intervals.
Recomputed examples: 1000/(120-100)=50 seconds; 10,000*5=50,000 outputs/s; 10,000/2,000=5-second mean; 2.4M/(10k-8k)=1,200 seconds.
Recomputed exercises: 300/(250-190)=5 seconds and doubled buffer 10; 4,000*3.5=14,000/s and *600=8.4 MB/s.
Recomputed 6,000/1,500=4-second mean; 18M/(25k-20k)=3,600 seconds; equal capacity gives zero net drain.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Fluid/discrete arithmetic is illustrative and excludes stochastic tails, skew, checkpoint overhead, retries, and controller dynamics.

evidence: Verified constant lambda>mu yields cumulative excess (lambda-mu)t and fills any finite free capacity in finite time.
Checked end-to-end boundedness requires every hidden queue bounded plus feedback to a boundary that can slow, durably retain, or terminally handle excess.
Verified credit safety requires outstanding work no greater than issued unreturned credit backed by actual reserved capacity.
Checked recovery catch-up N/(mu-lambda) requires mu>lambda and does not converge for mu<=lambda.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Necessary stability conditions are not overstated as sufficient tail-latency guarantees under variable arrivals/service.

evidence: Reviewed sustained load below/at/above capacity, empty/full buffers, first/last credit, reconnect epochs, credit loss/duplication, cancellation, and control progress at saturation.
Reviewed short/long bursts, giant/compressed-expanding records, hot keys, asymmetric inputs, fan-out branch failure, head-of-line, and window/timer bursts.
Reviewed slow/ambiguous sinks, retries/timeouts/circuit break, layered retry storms, quota throttling, checkpoint pressure, failure/restore, and nonconverging catch-up.
Reviewed decompression bombs, forged priority/deadline, connection hoarding, sparse keepalives, tenant starvation, fan-out abuse, and telemetry exposure.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Memory boundedness, delivery, fairness, liveness, latency, checkpointability, recovery, and security are independently reviewed.

evidence: Traced offered work through weighted admission, parse/expansion, per-stage bounded queues/credits, async/state processing, fan-out, sink batching, retry, and terminal outcomes.
Checked each queue has count/byte/work/age/concurrency bounds, ownership, overflow, retry, persistence, fairness, and observability.
Checked pressure propagates opposite data flow to an actionable source/admission boundary without one hidden unbounded queue.
Checked recovery preserves source retention and has sustainable capacity above live arrivals while checkpoint/control paths retain reserved progress.
invariant_checking.notes: Application demand, runtime/network credits, TCP flow control, broker retention, admission, and shedding retain separate scopes.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from graph/queues and conservation through capacity, bounds, feedback, topology, overload, lifecycle, security/fairness, and evidence.
Checked finite-buffer impossibility proof and counterexample that doubling buffer doubles time but preserves persistent deficit.
Checked credit proof includes real resource backing, exact return point, and reconnect/owner fencing.
Checked end-to-end proof fails with any library, mailbox, retry, kernel, state, broker, or client queue left unbounded.
proof_review.notes: Generic queueing/flow arguments are separated from Flink, Spark, Kafka, Reactive Streams, and TCP mechanisms.

evidence: Audited uses of stable, bounded, durable, blocked, rejected, shed, completed, fair, sustainable, backpressured, and recovered.
Confirmed buffer sizing, Little's relation, service rate, utilization, flow conservation, and catch-up claims state steady/fluid/measurement assumptions.
Confirmed unaligned checkpoints, autoscaling, retries, batching, broker durability, TCP flow control, and load shedding are not mislabeled as capacity fixes.
Confirmed executable fixture disclaims stochastic behavior, priorities, distributed credits, transport, retries, checkpoints, and percentiles.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No absence of OOM or aggregate spare CPU is mislabeled as stable latency, fairness, or per-shard headroom.

evidence: Reviewed offered/admitted/completed/rejected/retried rates in records/bytes/work plus queue count/bytes/age, credits, in-flight work, service, and task-state metrics.
Reviewed correlations with source lag, watermark/state/timers, buffer/mailbox, CPU/GC/disk/network, checkpoint delay/bytes, external quotas/errors, autoscaling, and freshness.
Confirmed no universal queue/credit/batch/concurrency/retry limit, utilization target, fairness weight, timeout, shedding rule, or scaling threshold is prescribed.
Confirmed production decisions require sustained/burst/skew/failure experiments with checkpoints/telemetry enabled and semantic/result/cost evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The local conservation fixture is not production evidence for throughput, tail latency, controller stability, or delivery semantics.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed queue inventory/conservation, stability/bursts, demand/credits, buffer bounds, bottleneck localization, expansion/skew, multi-input/fan-out, async/batch/retry, source admission, overload outcomes, checkpoints/watermarks, recovery/catch-up, controllers, fairness/security, observability, and validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed whole-path queue mapping, multi-unit capacity, per-shard diagnosis, credit epochs/control reserves, async/batch/retry bounds, source pause, explicit overload semantics, tenant fairness, checkpoint-enabled baselines, catch-up headroom, controller interaction, telemetry, and fault/load experiments. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from queue conservation and stability through graph mechanisms and operations. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover fill time, expansion, Little's relation, credits, batching, fairness, fan-out, catch-up, checkpoint interactions, executable conservation, and production review.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Reactive Streams/Flink/Spark/Kafka/TCP maintainer, queueing/network/distributed-systems researcher, data/storage/sink engineer, SRE/performance/capacity specialist, security/fairness/tenant owner, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
